state.context: CanTable is a draft host-controlled hospitality app. Cafe, Table and Booking currently inherit default D1; the requirements prose nevertheless requests Durable Objects. Imported employee.can_work scans mutable Employee rows in D1. DESIGN permits only one storage authority per mutation and rejects cross-owner decision reads; binding Cafe to a DO would violate this without a versioned local work-grant projection. No such projection exists. D1 already has a shared optimistic revision fence. Adoption, simple source and token economy matter, and no runtime implementation is in scope. The proposed workflow retains reservation from/until, adds estimated_until for seating, blocks seating while an earlier party is physically uncleared, admits nonoverlapping future reservations independently of current occupancy, flags due/estimate-overlapping/overdue conflicts, and records required reasons when moving or cancelling confirmed reservations. Active reservations or physical occupants prevent table deactivation and insufficient capacity; historical cleared parties do not constrain current capacity. Source invariants cover shared paths and host history attributes changes. Component text/details show the affected reservation rows; there is no authored Badge/Alert primitive.

placement.instructions: Choose the storage design that makes the stated workflows valid under current language ownership rules while balancing contention and implementation/source burden.

criteria.d1: Revise the draft DO requirement to the existing D1 authority, keeping live employee eligibility and hospitality writes within its revision fence; accept possible database-wide contention.
criteria.do: Retain per-café DO authority and first design a versioned local employee-eligibility projection and its revocation behavior; gain per-owner concurrency while increasing language/source and integration work.

workflow.instructions: Does the proposed business model preserve real occupancy, explicit conflict resolution and reservation editing without silently rewriting confirmed commitments or freezing historical table capacity?
